name: bug-feet-lock-pop
description: Lock feet used to hold the ankle at the contact's mean place in all three directions, so a heel that rose was forced down into the floor and the leg stretched, and the knee popped on release (Walk 15: 2.17 to 7.73 m/s). It now holds the ball of the foot across the floor only. Standing keys at 0 and 30, the second 0.1 hip heights along +X (8.7 cm, 0.087 m/s, under the 0.5 m/s contact limit): both feet are in contact on all 31 frames and each slides 8.7 cm. Locking changes all 31 frames, then plants the 28 between the keys as well (`frames` counts both: 59), and the slide goes to about 0, each foot held at its mean place. The keys stay flat on the floor, so no joint changes speed by over 1 m/s.
